parenting styles, child academic characteristics, and child personal characteristics all play a role in child academic achievement.

parenting practices, specifically parental monitoring and involvement in school, are positively associated with academic success in middle school children, and that children with high self efficacy and low levels of self-regulated learning benefit from high levels of parent involvement in school.

parental monitoring and involvement with school related activities is positively associated with academic outcomes, although involvement with school related homework is negatively associated with academic outcomes.

how parents can best support their children in their academic achievement and what factors are associated with child academic achievement.
the role of parenting practices and child factors in determining child academic achievement.
how parents influence the outcomes in their child's lives, and the factors that can either buffer or mediate these effects.

parenting styles, parental monitoring and involvement, as well as child characteristics, all play an important role in child academic achievement.

parental involvement in children's academic lives is an important predictor in academic achievement, but other factors such as child characteristics may be protective or detrimental to academic achievement, depending on the child and the parenting style.

parents can have a positive influence on their children's academic achievement, although the influence of parenting practices may be moderated by child characteristics and mediate by child academic characteristics.
